newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreign firms eye Brazil Cerj sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms eye Brazil Cerj sell-off.

text.p: Chilean, French and local firms have showed interest in Rio de Janeiro state's electricity distributor Cerj, due to be privatized on November 20, an official at the power firm.

Claudio Bentes, Cerj's financial director, said 10 large domestic and foreign operators have already consulted and visited the company, including local power firms Light and Escelsa, and France's EDF.
Chilean power firm Chilectra and Brazilian private bank Bozano, Simonsen are expected to visit the firm this week, he added.
Rio de Janeiro state will sell off its 78 percent stake in Cerj for a minimum price of 499 million reais. Up to 10 million reais of the sale price could be paid in privatization bonds.

Company employees are currently allowed to buy 10 percent of the share capital held by the state, equivalent to 7.8 percent of the total share capital, with a 30 percent discount on the minimum price. The offer for employees expires on Nov 18.
The remaining 70.3 percent of shares will be sold off in one single block during an auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ) for the minimum price of 464.7 million reais.

The tender documents state that any consortium interested in acquiring Cerj will have to include a power operator. The operator must have at least one million customers, sales of at least 5,000 gigawatts and less than 12 percent energy losses.
According to the firm's privatization process, investors will have to pre-qualify by next Monday.

Cerj accounts for 19 percent of the electricity distributed in Rio de Janeiro state and serves around 1.2 million customers. It had losses of 122.2 million reais in the first half. Cerj's financial director said he expects to release the company's third quarter results before the auction.
